items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-products-homotopy at source lines 4908-4925, three statements about products: finitely many homotopy equivalences between the factors give a homotopy equivalence of the products; a family of homotopies between the factor maps gives a homotopy between the product maps; and in the finite case the converse holds, namely a homotopy between the product maps gives homotopies between the factors. The proof at source lines 4927-4949 is a genuine write-out of the homotopy data. Part (2) has to package the given homotopies into a single homotopy between the product morphisms, which means carrying, in each degree, a map from the product of the X_t into the next degree of the product of the Y_t, and verifying the homotopy identity component by component. Part (3) is the converse and requires extracting from a homotopy between the product maps a homotopy for each factor, which uses that the finite product admits the canonical projections and that a map into a product is determined by its components; the finiteness hypothesis is what lets the extraction be carried out degree by degree. The statement lists the conclusions and none of the extraction or packaging argument. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
